name: riften::Thiefpool (ConorWilliams/Threadpool)
workload: Matrix multiplication (8x8 to 1024x1024) split into tasks on the pool, measured with nanobench in a third-party pool comparison.
claimed_speedup: Clang results: Thiefpool at 98.3-99.0% relative to the reference pool versus 90.2-94.5% for BS::thread_pool, e.g. 1024x1024: 52.80 ms/op vs 57.14 ms/op, about 8% faster (derived from page data). MSVC 256x256: 93.18 ms vs 99.73 ms.
compiler_and_flags: Clang and MSVC; flags not stated
hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X, 32 GB RAM, Windows (Clang via WSL)
tradeoffs: C++20 only; lock-free riften::Deque work stealing; enqueue returns std::future (enqueue_detach avoids the shared state allocation); MPL-2.0 file-level copyleft.
caveats: The only numbers are from another pool's README benchmark (dp::thread_pool), not from the project itself; the repo has no benchmark of its own. Compiler flags not stated, Windows machine with noted frequency scaling, error margins up to 1.4%. Differences are small and BS::thread_pool is not TBB, OpenMP or Rayon. The same results show Thiefpool within about 1-8% of dp::thread_pool, so it is not a clear winner.
found_via: Package registries (vcpkg, conan, crates.io, pkg.go.dev, PyPI): WebSearch 'riften Thiefpool lock-free work stealing thread pool C++ benchmark'; CPM-installable per its README
